status: Rejected after two GPU rounds: correct but slower on every scored shape
observed_bottleneck: Marlin GEMMs are about65percent of fused decoder profile GPU time; current alternatives slower. Native split-K uses serialized global FP32 reduction with workspace locks.
candidate_design: Use own copied, renamed Marlin template, preserving Apache2copyright. Never alter installed/loaded modules.
Accumulate raw fragment c0/c1 into caller-owned zeroed FP32 output via atomicAdd, instead of serialized split-K reduction. Do not use existing BF16 atomic mode, which lowers reduction precision.
Keep original BF16 activations and NVFP4 storage. Finalize FP32 sum to BF16 and global scale with native rounding semantics after inspecting prepare_moe_nvfp4_layer_for_marlin.
Use original per-slot local expert IDs to select per-expert global scale in finalization. Both GEMMs receive current-call local IDs.

Remove native atomic BF16 output writes and its initialization/wait protocol only in own template; launch with use_atomic_add=True to bypass serialized reduction. Caller zeros FP32 accumulator every call.
Own namespace avoids loaded-module changes. Existing custom launch wrapper can dispatch copied template; native helper includes remain installed.
